notes: NCBI StatPearls Behcet Disease was reread for recurrent oral/genital aphthae, uveitis, pathergy, arterial and venous disease of variable caliber, thrombosis, and neutrophil-predominant vascular pathology.
NCBI Systemic Vasculitis and the Chapel Hill definition table were reread for the multisystem clinical spectrum and the formal characterization of Behçet vasculitis as affecting arteries or veins.
NCBI Vasculitis guidance was reread for the characteristic clinical cluster and differential separation from other vasculitides.
The official USMLE Content Outline 2026 explicitly lists Behçet syndrome under Multisystem Processes & Disorders — immunologic and inflammatory disorders.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.syndrome: The recurrent oral aphthae, scar-forming genital ulcers, relapsing uveitis, pathergy and venous thrombosis are all recognized Behçet manifestations.
claim_audit.variable_vessel_scope: Authoritative sources define Behçet as systemic vasculitis that can involve both arteries and veins across vessel sizes.
claim_audit.histopathology: Active mucocutaneous/vascular lesions commonly show a neutrophil-predominant vascular reaction, endothelial injury and thrombosis; older lesions may be more lymphocytic.
claim_audit.pathergy: A sterile papule/pustule after minor needle trauma is a characteristic pathergy reaction and strongly supports Behçet in the appropriate clinical setting.
claim_audit.thrombosis: Venous thrombosis, including superficial thrombophlebitis and DVT, is a recognized vascular manifestation of Behçet.
claim_audit.distractor_1: Giant cell arteritis is a granulomatous medium/large-artery vasculitis with multinucleated giant cells and does not explain the oral/genital/uveitic/pathergy syndrome.
claim_audit.distractor_2: IgA vasculitis is a small-vessel immune-complex disease characterized by IgA deposition and typically palpable purpura with renal/GI/joint involvement, not the Behçet pattern.
claim_audit.distractor_3: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis centers on necrotizing granulomatous respiratory disease and pauci-immune glomerulonephritis, which are absent.
claim_audit.distractor_4: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis requires the asthma/eosinophilic phenotype and has different histopathology.
claim_audit.blueprint_claim: USMLE 2026 explicitly names Behçet syndrome in Multisystem Processes & Disorders.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The diagnosis is Behçet syndrome from recurrent oral/genital aphthae, uveitis and pathergy. The new DVT is not a separate incidental thrombophilia clue; Behçet itself commonly causes inflammatory venous thrombosis and can also affect arteries. The most fitting pathology is variable-vessel neutrophilic vasculitis with thrombosis.
adversarial_second_pass.thrombophilia_challenge: Factor V Leiden, prothrombin mutation, antiphospholipid syndrome and other thrombophilias can produce DVT, but they do not explain pathergy plus recurrent mucocutaneous and ocular inflammation. No coagulation-genetic claim is needed to answer this item.
adversarial_second_pass.iga_vasculitis_challenge: Both diseases can involve skin and vessels, but IgA vasculitis is a small-vessel immune-complex syndrome with palpable purpura, abdominal/joint/renal disease; the oral/genital/uveitis/pathergy combination is not its phenotype.
adversarial_second_pass.gpa_challenge: GPA can cause systemic vasculitis but requires a different respiratory/renal/granulomatous constellation. The vignette deliberately contains no sinus, pulmonary or glomerular features.
adversarial_second_pass.egpa_challenge: EGPA is not competitive without asthma, eosinophilia or eosinophilic disease.
adversarial_second_pass.giant_cell_challenge: Age and clinical phenotype strongly exclude giant cell arteritis, and Behçet is not restricted to arterial disease.
adversarial_second_pass.histology_nuance: Behçet histology is not one immutable pattern in every lesion. The keyed answer uses 'neutrophil-predominant vasculitis with thrombosis that can involve...' rather than claiming every affected vessel must show identical histology.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All options describe genuine vasculitic/pathologic patterns of comparable specificity. The correct answer is not simply the disease name and does not contain a unique eponym.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: The item avoids classification-score thresholds, HLA frequencies, pathergy sensitivity/specificity, age/geographic prevalence, and thrombosis incidence.
